title: Broncos OC Davis Webb, when asked last month about the team's offensive philosophy as he goes into his first season as primary play-caller: "I think we'll kind of feel that as we go. I think the Rams are the best example; they went until Week 6, and they started playing a lot more heavy, 13 personnel. I think we'll grow and adapt as the season goes. That's everywhere I've been. But we have a pretty good idea of where we've been with Bo (Nix) the last couple of years, and what's been successful. Like, we started in February as a coaching staff, 'Hey, let's look at the last two years since Bo's taken over, and what are we good at? What do we need to re-look at?' And what's going on around the league and who we play. So, it's been a combination of a lot of things. Some new ideas -- especially in the spring to kind of get off the ground and kind of see where everything is at, but once we get to the season, we'll have a better idea."

title: Former Cardinals TE Travis Vokolek announced his retirement from football today. The 28-year-old announced his decision in a post on Instagram. He said he was advised to medically retire by doctor and neurologists after he suffered a neck injury during a kickoff in the first quarter of the Cardinals’ Week 6 game at the Indianapolis Colts. He was carted off the field and was sent to a local hospital after the injury before being out on IR for the rest of the season. Vokolek was a UDFA in 2023 out of Nebraska.

title: Tom is infuriatingly good at his job. No one understands the complex world of the NFL from contracts to labor laws to the NFLPA to owners to hiring cycles, free agency, trades and everything in-between better than him. But to be able to digest all of that information and then articulate it in a way that allows every single NFL fan to understand what is going on is his true superpower. But that's work. Which obviously is a huge part of our lives. And how our personal lives and work overlap creates a sort of work family. We know everything about each other's kids. Our wives go on girls trips together. We've created relationships that go far beyond work colleagues. That's what makes moves like this so difficult to understand. Not just because Tom is outstanding at what he does, but because it's personal. Can't wait to see what he pours himself into next. Because I know how my friend is wired.

title: Bray Hubbard to @SXMCollege: "Coach Wommack called me after the season was over, and we were just talking about different things during the season and things that went wrong that were really just on us. When we really looked at it, it was guys not focusing on their job. "When you have all 11 guys that are doing their job -- which we had flashes of during the season and were playing at an extremely high level -- but when you have guys that are, say, I have this gap but this guy wants to stay in his gap and wants to jump over to mine, what good is that doing? You have two guys doing the same job. "That's what it kind of came down to, and that's been the focus all spring. Coach Wommack said it. He said, look, we're gonna put the best guys out there that are gonna execute and do their job. Because at the end of the day, everybody has their own role. You have to do that to the best of your ability, and if you're trying to do someone else's job, what good is that going to do you?"

title: Nick Sirianni on the WRs: "I think that I'm really excited about this receiver room. DeVonta Smith is just, he's a special player that can continue to get even more targets...He's so capable of doing even more, and he's phenomenal, he is such a good football player. "Then 'Tay Wicks has this great ability — gosh, there are so many similarities, and again, this is going to be a high praise statement and and I'm not saying he's this guy, but gosh, he reminds me of Keenan Allen ...with the way they are off the line of scrimmage, the way they are at the top of the route, with the way they are with the ball in their hands, he just really reminds me of him in that aspect. "Makai, obviously, we drafted him for a reason, where we drafted him. He has this ability to catch the football, and in tough situations. "I've liked Marquis Brown and Elijah Moore for a long time. I've really always admired their game of how they played, and it's just been nice to see them. They have these really special traits. To have our third, fourth receiver be these guys. I'm really excited about this room." ...He also likes the depth. Darius Cooper and Johnny Wilson give the dirty work profile that Sirianni craves. Quez Watkins and Danny Gray are players who've been around on the practice squad.

When asked about Jackson Lloyd named LT starter, DeBoer said, "You see the response that a kid like Jackson Lloyd has. A guy that -- your left tackle. There's levels of pressure that each guy has, and that tackle position is a perceived high-level, especially on the left side with a right-hand quarterback. The way he went about it -- Jackson never flinched the rest of spring. He just kept being who he was, and kept improving. He had that humility and that brought out another level of leadership in him, which we needed to have on that offensive line. "Michael Carroll and he and -- Michael's had a great summer, and expect him to have a great fall again as he continues to improve on what he did last year."

title: Kalen DeBoer to @977ESPN on Alabama O-line: "We aren't there yet. We got to have a great fall camp of really execution-wise, and I think that's what it comes down to is execution. Executing your individual footwork. Confidence in the guy next to you. You may know what you're doing and you may do your job well, but if you're just a little bit unsure of what the next guy's footwork is. We had a lot of new faces that were in the lineup. I think a lot of people think -- and sometimes it was, there were times when we moved people around to try to find the best group -- but also there were things that just injury-wise and/or other that just kept guys from being able to be on the football field or the reason why we had to put somebody else in those spots. That lack of continuity -- you try to make a positive out of it, but in the end, there's got to be some type of jelling of those guys up front to where one guy makes a call and it just gets relayed all the way down from one guy to another, from the enter on out, just to the tackles but to the tight ends and the running backs are all on the same page and they can envision what this play is going to look like and how the blocking scheme is going to match the front before it even happens."
